extracted.intended_audience: independent television producers and production companies (UK); Channel 4 commissioning and legal/commercial teams
extracted.subtask_description: A Code of Practice setting out Channel 4's minimum terms and procedures for commissioning programmes from Qualifying Independent Production Companies, including definitions of rights, licence periods, deal structures, pricing/tariff guidance, and processes for negotiation, monitoring and dispute resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity over categories of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity over the different categories of rights that Channel 4 is seeking to secure in programmes it commissions from independent producers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Code commits to clearly defining Core Rights and Secondary Rights and to publish a more detailed legal definition of these rights to Producers; Channel 4 may review definitions over time to reflect market developments and new distribution technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity over duration of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity over the duration for which Channel 4 seeks to secure these different categories of rights
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Channel 4 will move from acquiring rights in perpetuity to licensing Core Rights for defined licence periods (see Licence Periods entry). Duration expectations are part of minimum terms offered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity over prices to be paid
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity over the prices that Channel 4 is willing to pay for these different categories of rights
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Channel 4 will regularly publish an indicative tariff of prices it expects to pay for Core Rights to enable Producers to assess relative value; final price determined via editorial specification review and possibly budget review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear commissioning process and reasonable timetable
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear commissioning process with a reasonable timetable for negotiations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Code emphasises transparency of the commissioning process and sets expectations around communication and timeliness of negotiations (see separate headings: Transparency of Process, Communication with Producers, Timeliness of Negotiations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisions for monitoring application and dispute resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions for monitoring the application of this Code and resolving any disputes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Channel 4 commits to internal review, accountability and arbitration procedures (see headings: Monitoring the Application of Channel 4’s Code of Practice; Internal Review and Accountability; Arbitration of Disputes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and applicability of the Code
rubrics_metrics.description: This Code applies to all commissioned programmes from Qualifying Independent Production Companies by Channel 4’s core public service channel, with specified exceptions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include programmes commissioned by 4 Learning (different rights approach), Channel 4's digital channels, feature film commissioning activity (which will not be subject to the detail of this Code), and cases where Channel 4 or 4 Ventures develops formats internally (Channel 4 may depart from Code positions in such cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Core Rights (exclusive)
rubrics_metrics.description: Channel 4 defines the exclusive Core Rights it requires from any programme commissioned as: rights to transmit on core Channel 4 in the UK & Republic of Ireland (including catch-up); rights for contemporaneous programme support services targeted at UK & ROI; rights for exploitation of the programme format in the UK & ROI; ability to exercise a holdback on rights to exploit the programme on any platform targeted at the secondary transmission market in the UK & ROI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Channel 4 will publish a more detailed legal definition of Core Rights; it reserves the right to review categorisation for new distribution technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Secondary Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: All rights not currently falling within the Core Rights definition are Secondary Rights
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secondary Rights include, but are not limited to, international distribution rights via any media platform and Consumer Products rights (e.g. video, publishing, merchandising) in the UK and internationally; terms and licence durations for Secondary Rights will be negotiated separately and on a case-by-case basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licence periods for Core Rights (duration and extensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Rights will be licensed for a defined duration on an exclusive basis: for as long as Channel 4 is commissioning the programme and for a 5-year period thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Channel 4 will require an automatic option to extend the licence for an additional two years upon payment to the Producer of an advance equivalent to 2 off-peak repeats payments. Any extension beyond that should be achieved through commercial negotiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability timing for Secondary Rights (UK vs international)
rubrics_metrics.description: Secondary Rights outside the United Kingdom will be available for immediate exploitation; Secondary Rights inside the United Kingdom will be available for exploitation following the first transmission of the programme (or entire series) on Channel 4, unless mutually agreed otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duration and other terms for any Secondary Rights acquired by 4 Rights will be negotiated separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deal structure — Option 1: Licence-only model
rubrics_metrics.description: Channel 4 acquires Core Rights for the licence period with holdback on further exploitation in the UK secondary TV market during the licence period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under this option Channel 4 acquires control of Core Rights enabling broadcast on its Core Service, retains exclusivity in the UK television market (no sales to third party channels in UK secondary market during licence), and the Producer retains control of Secondary Rights (may discuss exploitation with 4 Rights). Revenues from Secondary Rights are subject to revenue share principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deal structure — Option 2: Licence plus exploitation in UK secondary market
rubrics_metrics.description: Channel 4 acquires Core Rights and waives its holdback so Channel 4 (via 4 Rights) can exploit the programme in the UK secondary TV market during the licence period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Channel 4 acquires Core Rights for the licence period; Channel 4 waives holdback and may distribute via 4 Rights to channels where it has an interest or to third party channels in the multi-channel market; revenues are shared between Producer and Channel 4 subject to principles outlined in the Code. Producers retain control of Secondary Rights generally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision for alternative deal structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Channel 4 is willing to discuss a range of alternative deal structures that the Producer may prefer, and the choice of alternative deal structures is entirely at the discretion of the Producer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include continuing under Channel 4’s previous terms of trade where Channel 4 would exploit Core and Secondary rights on behalf of the Producer. Details are subject to commercial negotiation and contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producers' freedom to exploit Secondary Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Producers who have licenced Core Rights to Channel 4 will have complete freedom as to how they wish to exploit the Secondary Rights and will be under no obligation to discuss or accept a commercial relationship with the Corporation for the exploitation of these rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producers may discuss Secondary Rights with any distributor at any point, including before approaching Channel 4 about Core Rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arm's-length negotiation for 4 Rights and non-conditioning of Core offers
rubrics_metrics.description: Negotiation for the acquisition of Secondary Rights by 4 Rights will be conducted at arm’s length from Channel 4’s negotiations regarding Core Rights; no offer for Core Rights by Channel 4 will ever be conditional on 4 Rights securing Secondary Rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 4 Rights will expect to be treated no more, or less, favourably by the Producer than any other distributor; Channel 4 will not adjust relative prices to improve the position of Channel 4/4 Rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a single contract for efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid increasing Channel 4’s cost base and to retain operational efficiencies (e.g. clearances) the Corporation will use a single contract to encompass all rights issues relating to a given commissioned programme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is intended to reduce bureaucracy while not conditioning commercial independence of Secondary Rights negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: UK format rights handling and return after 'dark' period
rubrics_metrics.description: UK format rights are included within the Core Rights package to protect against similar programmes appearing on competitive UK channels, but Channel 4 will not warehouse UK format rights if a programme has not been re-commissioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Channel 4 will return format rights to the Producer following a 'dark' period of 12 months, at which point the Producer may exploit these rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of an indicative tariff of prices
rubrics_metrics.description: Channel 4 will regularly publish an indicative tariff of the prices it expects to pay for Core Rights to enable Producers to assess the relative value of Core Rights for a potential commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tariff will establish a range of indicative prices reflecting cost variations by genre and day-part (primarily Peak vs. Off-Peak). It is an initial indication; the final price will be determined via detailed discussion of editorial specification and sometimes a budget review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors influencing value of Core Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The value of Core Rights to Channel 4 will be influenced by a range of factors, including but not limited to genre and day-part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tariff and final pricing consider programme-specific editorial specification and budget; other market or programme factors may also influence price (full factors list is to be published/expanded by Channel 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Producer responsibility for deficit finance and options via 4 Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the price paid by Channel 4 for Core Rights is insufficient to fund production costs (deficit finance), it is the Producer's responsibility to secure the additional funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producers can seek to access required funding through a commercial relationship with 4 Rights regarding exploitation of Secondary Rights; details subject to negotiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and separate negotiations for Core vs Secondary Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Service Broadcasters should offer separate prices for Core and Secondary Rights and enter into separate, transparent negotiations to acquire different categories of rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Channel 4's approach is to provide separate, transparent negotiations and pricing for Core and Secondary Rights, consistent with ITC recommendations and Communications Act obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to review and adapt rights definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Channel 4 reserves the right to review rights definitions from time to time to take account of significant market developments and to establish appropriate categorisation for any new distribution technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This signals that the Core/Secondary Rights lists are not static and may be updated to reflect technological and market change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of negotiations and communication with producers
rubrics_metrics.description: Channel 4 commits to transparency of process and communication with Producers and to timeliness of negotiations (listed Code headings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While detailed procedures are set out elsewhere in the Code and in Terms of Trade to be published with PACT, the Code establishes an expectation of professional, timely dealings so Producers 'find Channel 4 professional and timely to do business with.'
